# Docker Agent examples as Pulumi programs

<!-- Generated by `make generate_config_types` (provider/internal/examplegen). Do not edit. -->

Every example configuration that [docker-agent v1.152.0](https://github.com/docker/docker-agent/tree/v1.152.0/examples) ships (202 YAML and 3 HCL files) as a Pulumi program in TypeScript and in Python, 203 programs per language. Each program builds the configuration with the `AgentConfig` resource and typed inputs only (no `extra`, no raw YAML), and keeps the comments of the upstream file, so the programs document the inputs the same way the upstream examples document the YAML.

The programs are generated from the docker-agent version in `provider/go.mod` by `make generate_config_types`, so they follow every docker-agent upgrade. Do not edit them; change `provider/internal/examplegen` instead. To turn your own agent files into programs like these, in any Pulumi language, use the converter: see [Converting existing agent files](https://github.com/dirien/pulumi-docker-agent/blob/main/docs/installation-configuration.md#converting-existing-agent-files).

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`typescript/`](typescript) | One Pulumi project. `examples/<name>.ts` builds one example; `index.ts` imports all of them and exports the stack output `configs` (example name → rendered YAML). |
| [`python/`](python) | The same in Python: `examples/<module>.py` and `__main__.py`. |
| [`testdata/`](testdata) | `<name>.yaml`: the YAML each program renders. `make test_examples` runs both projects and compares every value of `configs` with these files. |

## Running the examples

The projects use the provider and the SDKs built from this repository: `plugins.providers` points at `../../../bin`, and the SDK dependency at the build under `../../../sdk`.

```bash
# From the repository root
make provider build_nodejs        # or build_python

cd examples/docker-agent-examples/typescript    # or python
export PULUMI_BACKEND_URL="file://$HOME/.pulumi-local" PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE=local
pulumi stack init dev
pulumi install --no-plugins
pulumi up
```

Write one configuration to a file and run it with docker-agent:

```bash
pulumi stack output configs --json | jq -r '.["pirate"]' > pirate.yaml
docker agent run pirate.yaml
```

To use one example on its own, copy `typescript/examples/<name>.ts` as the `index.ts` of a TypeScript project (it exports `config` and `yaml`), or `python/examples/<module>.py` as the `__main__.py` of a Python project and add `pulumi.export("yaml", config.yaml)`. Outside this repository, install `@ediri/pulumi-docker-agent` or `ediri_docker_agent` and drop the `plugins` block from `Pulumi.yaml`.

Some examples refer to files that must be next to the YAML where docker-agent runs it, for example the documents of the RAG examples or the files of `instruction_file`. The programs keep those paths as they are.

## How the YAML maps to the programs

- Every key is a typed input: camelCase in TypeScript, snake_case in Python. Map keys (model names, environment variables, ...) and free-form values (JSON schemas, provider options, flavors) stay as written.
- YAML shorthands are written in their typed form, as docker-agent reads them: an `instruction` list is one string joined with blank lines, `skills: true` is `skills: ["local"]`, a `commands` list is one map, a `task_budget` object is its total, and a duration in seconds is a `"<n>s"` string.
- YAML anchors become variables: an alias is a reference to the variable, and a `<<` merge key is a spread (`...name` in TypeScript, `**name` in Python). See `yaml-anchors` ([TypeScript](typescript/examples/yaml-anchors.ts), [Python](python/examples/yaml_anchors.py)).
- Comments are carried over, next to the input they describe. Editor and shell directives (`# yaml-language-server` modelines and `#!` lines at the top of a file) are not.
- Multi-line strings are template literals (TypeScript) and triple-quoted strings (Python) whose lines start at column 0, so they hold exactly the text of the YAML block.
- The programs are formatted the way Prettier (`--tab-width 4 --print-width 100`) and Black (with its defaults) format them.
- `instruction_file` ([TypeScript](typescript/examples/instruction_file.ts), [Python](python/examples/instruction_file.py)) sets `skipValidation`: `instruction_file` reads files relative to the agent file. The provider validates the rendered YAML in memory.
- `rag-hybrid` ([TypeScript](typescript/examples/rag-hybrid.ts), [Python](python/examples/rag_hybrid.py)), `rag-reranking` ([TypeScript](typescript/examples/rag-reranking.ts), [Python](python/examples/rag_reranking.py)) leave out `batch_size`: docker-agent does not read the RAG strategy parameter `batch_size` (the number of chunks per embedding request is `embedding_batch_size`). A comment in each program shows the upstream line.
- [`gopher.hcl`](https://github.com/docker/docker-agent/blob/v1.152.0/examples/gopher.hcl) is the same configuration as `gopher.yaml` in HCL (docker-agent loads both identically), so `gopher` ([TypeScript](typescript/examples/gopher.ts), [Python](python/examples/gopher.py)) covers it.
- [`pirate.hcl`](https://github.com/docker/docker-agent/blob/v1.152.0/examples/pirate.hcl) is the same configuration as `pirate.yaml` in HCL (docker-agent loads both identically), so `pirate` ([TypeScript](typescript/examples/pirate.ts), [Python](python/examples/pirate.py)) covers it.
- `instructions_from_file` ([TypeScript](typescript/examples/instructions_from_file.ts), [Python](python/examples/instructions_from_file.py)) has no YAML version. It reads its `instruction` from `instructions_from_file.md` with docker-agent's `file()` helper, which renders the file as a template. The programs read a copy of the file next to them instead and replace its `${name}` placeholders the same way.
